---
title: Installation
guide-section: "Getting started"
---

trialforge targets Python 3.10+. Once it is released on PyPI:

```bash
pip install "trialforge[pl]"
```

Until then, install it from GitHub. This compiles the Rust engine from source, so it needs a Rust
toolchain (1.88 or later; [rustup](https://rustup.rs) is the easiest way to get one), and the
first build takes a few minutes:

```bash
pip install "trialforge[pl] @ git+https://github.com/rich-iannone/trialforge#subdirectory=python"
```

With uv, use `uv pip install` or `uv add` with the same requirement.

## Optional extras

The package itself has no Python dependencies. Datasets come back as DataFrames, so install a
backend with an extra; writing files needs none.

| Extra | Adds |
|---|---|
| `pl` | Polars, the default `output=` |
| `pd` | pandas (with PyArrow, which the conversion goes through) |
| `pa` | PyArrow |
| `verify`{.gd-no-link} | Pointblank, for `Study.verify(level=3)` |

If the backend for the `output=` you ask for is missing, the error names the extra that installs it.

## Wheels

Released wheels cover Python 3.10 and later (one abi3 wheel per platform) on Linux (x86_64 and
aarch64), macOS (Intel and Apple silicon) and Windows (x86_64). Elsewhere pip builds from the
source distribution, which needs the same Rust toolchain.

## R

The R package is built on the same engine and gives byte-identical data for the same request. See
its [documentation](../r/index.html) for installation and usage.
